sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ tava rājendra vairasyāsya samudbhavaḥ putraṃ te kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā kālayogena kāritaḥ
english: Before your very eyes, O king of kings, the origin of this enmity arose; with your son made its instrument, it was brought about by the working of Time.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ bhavitavye ca kurūṇāṃ vaiśase nṛpa kasmāc chocasi tāñ śūrān gatān paramikāṃ gatim
english: Since the slaughter of the Kurus was bound to come to pass, O king, why do you grieve for those heroes who have gone to the highest goal?

sanskrit: jānatā ca mahābāho vidureṇa mahātmanā yatitaṃ sarvayatnena śamaṃ prati janeśvara
english: And the great-souled Vidura, knowing all this, O mighty-armed lord of men, strove with every effort toward peace.

sanskrit: na ca daivakṛto mārgaḥ śakyo bhūtena kena cit ghaṭatāpi ciraṃ kālaṃ niyantum iti me matiḥ
english: Yet the course ordained by fate cannot be checked by any living being, however long one may strive against it: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ hi yat kāryaṃ mayā pratyakṣataḥ śrutam tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi kathaṃ sthairyaṃ bhavet tava
english: What task the gods had to accomplish I heard with my own ears; that I shall now relate to you fully, so that your firmness may return.

sanskrit: purāhaṃ tvarito yātaḥ sabhām aindrīṃ jitaklamaḥ apaśyaṃ tatra ca tadā samavetān divaukasaḥ nāradapramukhāṃś cāpi sarvān devaṛṣīṃs tathā
english: Once, having mastered all weariness, I went in haste to the assembly hall of Indra, and there I beheld the dwellers of heaven gathered together, and all the divine sages with Nārada at their head.

sanskrit: tatra cāpi mayā dṛṣṭā pṛthivī pṛthivīpate kāryārtham upasaṃprāptā devatānāṃ samīpataḥ
english: And there too, O lord of the earth, I saw the Earth herself, come into the presence of the gods upon an urgent errand.

sanskrit: upagamya tadā dhātrī devān āha samāgatān yat kāryaṃ mama yuṣmābhir brahmaṇaḥ sadane tadā pratijñātaṃ mahābhāgās tac chīghraṃ saṃvidhīyatām
english: Then the nourishing Earth, approaching the assembled gods, said: 'The task that you promised me in the abode of Brahmā, O most fortunate ones, let that now be swiftly accomplished.'

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā viṣṇur lokanamaskṛtaḥ uvāca prahasan vākyaṃ pṛthivīṃ devasaṃsadi
english: Hearing her words, Viṣṇu, to whom all the worlds bow down, smiled and spoke these words to the Earth in the council of the gods.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāṇāṃ yas tu jyeṣṭhaḥ śatasya vai duryodhana iti khyātaḥ sa te kāryaṃ kariṣyati taṃ ca prāpya mahīpālaṃ kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyasi
english: 'The eldest of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's hundred sons, renowned by the name Duryodhana, he shall accomplish your task; and through that guardian of the earth you shall attain your purpose.'

sanskrit: tasyārthe pṛthivīpālāḥ kurukṣetre samāgatāḥ anyonyaṃ ghātayiṣyanti dṛḍhaiḥ śastraiḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: 'For his sake the protectors of the earth, gathered together at Kurukṣetra, smiters all, shall slay one another with mighty weapons.'

sanskrit: tatas te bhavitā devi bhārasya yudhi nāśanam gaccha śīghraṃ svakaṃ sthānaṃ lokān dhāraya śobhane
english: 'Then, O goddess, your burden shall be destroyed in that battle; go swiftly to your own place, and uphold the worlds, O fair one.'

sanskrit: sa eṣa te suto rājaṃl lokasaṃhārakāraṇāt kaler aṃśaḥ samutpanno gāndhāryā jaṭhare nṛpa
english: This son of yours, O king, was born for the destruction of the world, sprung from a portion of Kali in the womb of Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: amarṣī capalaś cāpi krodhano duṣprasādhanaḥ daivayogāt samutpannā bhrātaraś cāsya tādṛśāḥ
english: Intolerant, fickle, prone to wrath, and hard to appease was he; and through the working of fate his brothers too were born of like nature.

sanskrit: śakunir mātulaś caiva karṇaś ca paramaḥ sakhā samutpannā vināśārthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ sahitā nṛpāḥ etam arthaṃ mahābāho nārado veda tattvataḥ
english: His maternal uncle Śakuni, and Karṇa his dearest friend, and the kings allied with them, were all born for the destruction of the earth. This matter, O mighty-armed one, Nārada knows in its very truth.

sanskrit: ātmāparādhāt putrās te vinaṣṭāḥ pṛthivīpate mā tāñ śocasva rājendra na hi śoke 'sti kāraṇam
english: By their own fault, O lord of the earth, your sons have perished; do not grieve for them, O king of kings, for there is no cause for grief.

sanskrit: na hi te pāṇḍavāḥ svalpam aparādhyanti bhārata putrās tava durātmāno yair iyaṃ ghātitā mahī
english: For the Pāṇḍavas have offended in nothing, however small, O Bhārata; it was your evil-souled sons by whom this earth was brought to ruin.

sanskrit: nāradena ca bhadraṃ te pūrvam eva na saṃśayaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya samitau rājasūye niveditam
english: And by Nārada, blessings upon you, this was foretold long before, beyond all doubt, in the assembly of Yudhiṣṭhira at the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāḥ kauravāś caiva samāsādya parasparam na bhaviṣyanti kaunteya yat te kṛtyaṃ tad ācara
english: 'The Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas, having come to clash with one another, shall cease to be, O son of Kuntī; therefore do what is to be done.'

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā tadāśocanta pāṇḍavāḥ etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ devaguhyaṃ sanātanam
english: Hearing Nārada's words, the Pāṇḍavas grieved even then. All this, the eternal secret of the gods, I have now told you in full.

sanskrit: kathaṃ te śokanāśaḥ syāt prāṇeṣu ca dayā prabho snehaś ca pāṇḍuputreṣu jñātvā daivakṛtaṃ vidhim
english: How may your grief be destroyed, O lord, and compassion for the living be restored, and tenderness toward the sons of Pāṇḍu, once you know that this was the decree ordained by fate?

sanskrit: eṣa cārtho mahābāho pūrvam eva mayā śrutaḥ kathito dharmarājasya rājasūye kratūttame
english: This matter, O mighty-armed one, I had heard long before, and I told it to the Dharma King at the Rājasūya, that most excellent of sacrifices.

sanskrit: yatitaṃ dharmaputreṇa mayā guhye nivedite avigrahe kauravāṇāṃ daivaṃ tu balavattaram
english: When I had disclosed the secret, the son of Dharma strove for peace among the Kauravas, that there might be no strife; but fate proved the stronger force.

sanskrit: anatikramaṇīyo hi vidhī rājan kathaṃ cana kṛtāntasya hi bhūtena sthāvareṇa trasena ca
english: For the decree of the Ordainer, O king, can in no way be transgressed by any being, whether unmoving or moving.

sanskrit: bhavān karmaparo yatra buddhiśreṣṭhaś ca bhārata muhyate prāṇināṃ jñātvā gatiṃ cāgatim eva ca
english: You, who are devoted to right action and foremost in wisdom, O Bhārata, are bewildered, though you know the coming and the going of all living creatures.

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu śokena saṃtaptaṃ muhyamānaṃ muhur muhuḥ jñātvā yudhiṣṭhiro rājā prāṇān api parityajet
english: But should King Yudhiṣṭhira learn that you are consumed by grief and swooning again and again, he might even cast away his very life.

sanskrit: kṛpālur nityaśo vīras tiryagyonigateṣv api sa kathaṃ tvayi rājendra kṛpāṃ vai na kariṣyati
english: That hero is ever compassionate even toward creatures born in the brute wombs; how then, O king of kings, should he fail to show compassion to you?

sanskrit: mama caiva niyogena vidheś cāpy anivartanāt pāṇḍavānāṃ ca kāruṇyāt prāṇān dhāraya bhārata
english: At my command, and because the decree of fate cannot be turned aside, and out of compassion for the Pāṇḍavas, hold fast to your life, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: evaṃ te vartamānasya loke kīrtir bhaviṣyati dharmaś ca sumahāṃs tāta taptaṃ syāc ca tapaś cirāt
english: Bearing yourself thus, you shall win renown in the world, and great merit, my son, and it shall be as though you had long performed austerities.

sanskrit: putraśokasamutpannaṃ hutāśaṃ jvalitaṃ yathā prajñāmbhasā mahārāja nirvāpaya sadā sadā
english: The fire of grief for your sons, blazing like a kindled flame, quench it ever and again, O great king, with the waters of wisdom.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ muhūrtaṃ samanudhyāya dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Hearing these words of Vyāsa of boundless splendor, Dhṛtarāṣṭra reflected for a moment and then spoke.

sanskrit: mahatā śokajālena praṇunno 'smi dvijottama nātmānam avabudhyāmi muhyamāno muhur muhuḥ
english: "By the great net of grief I am borne down, O best of the twice-born; swooning again and again, I cannot even know my own self."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā tava daivaniyogajam dhārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ prāṇān yatiṣye ca naśocitum
english: "But having heard these words of yours, born of the ordinance of fate, I shall hold fast to my life, and I shall strive to grieve no more."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rājendra tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Hearing these words of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O king of kings, Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, vanished then and there.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca gate bhagavati vyāse dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ kim aceṣṭata viprarṣe tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: Janamejaya said: When the blessed Vyāsa had departed, what did the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra do? O sage among brāhmaṇas, deign to explain this to me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā naraśreṣṭha ciraṃ dhyātvā tv acetanaḥ saṃjayaṃ yojayety uktvā viduraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, O best of men, and brooding long as if bereft of sense, he said, "Let Saṃjaya yoke the chariot," and then addressed Vidura.

sanskrit: kṣipram ānaya gāndhārīṃ sarvāś ca bharatastriyaḥ vadhūṃ kuntīm upādāya yāś cānyās tatra yoṣitaḥ
english: "Bring Gāndhārī quickly, and all the women of the Bharatas, taking with them the daughter-in-law Kuntī and whatever other women are there."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa dharmātmā viduraṃ dharmavittamam śokaviprahatajñāno yānam evānvapadyata
english: Having thus spoken to Vidura, foremost in the knowledge of dharma, that righteous king, his understanding shattered by grief, mounted his chariot.

sanskrit: gāndhārī caiva śokārtā bhartur vacanacoditā saha kuntyā yato rājā saha strībhir upādravat
english: And Gāndhārī, stricken with grief, urged by her husband's command, together with Kuntī and the other women, hastened to where the king was.

sanskrit: tāḥ samāsādya rājānaṃ bhṛśaṃ śokasamanvitāḥ āmantryānyonyam īyuḥ sma bhṛśam uccukruśus tataḥ
english: Reaching the king, overwhelmed with grief, calling out to one another they went forth, and then they wailed aloud most bitterly.

sanskrit: tāḥ samāśvāsayat kṣattā tābhyaś cārtataraḥ svayam aśrukaṇṭhīḥ samāropya tato 'sau niryayau purāt
english: Vidura sought to comfort them, though himself more stricken than they; and having mounted them, their throats choked with tears, upon the carriages, he set forth from the city.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇādaḥ saṃjajñe sarveṣu kuruveśmasu ākumāraṃ puraṃ sarvam abhavac chokakarśitam
english: Then a great outcry arose throughout all the dwellings of the Kurus; the whole city, down to its children, was wasted with grief.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvā yā nāryaḥ purā devagaṇair api pṛthagjanena dṛśyanta tās tadā nihateśvarāḥ
english: Women who had never before been seen even by the hosts of the gods were now beheld by common folk, their lords slain in battle.

sanskrit: prakīrya keśān suśubhān bhūṣaṇāny avamucya ca ekavastradharā nāryaḥ paripetur anāthavat
english: Their beautiful hair flung loose, their ornaments cast away, clad each in a single garment, the women ran about like the helpless and forlorn.

sanskrit: śvetaparvatarūpebhyo gṛhebhyas tās tv apākraman guhābhya iva śailānāṃ pṛṣatyo hatayūthapāḥ
english: From their mansions, white as snowy mountains, they hastened forth, like dappled does whose herd-leaders are slain fleeing the caverns of the hills.

sanskrit: tāny udīrṇāni nārīṇāṃ tadā vṛndāny anekaśaḥ śokārtāny adravan rājan kiśorīṇām ivāṅgane
english: Those manifold throngs of women, swelling forth and stricken with grief, ran about, O king, like fillies loosed in a paddock.

sanskrit: pragṛhya bāhūn krośantyaḥ putrān bhrātṝn pitṝn api darśayantīva tā ha sma yugānte lokasaṃkṣayam
english: Flinging up their arms and crying aloud for their sons, their brothers, and their fathers, they seemed to show forth the destruction of the world at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: vilapantyo rudantyaś ca dhāvamānās tatas tataḥ śokenābhyāhatajñānāḥ kartavyaṃ na prajajñire
english: Lamenting and weeping, running this way and that, their senses smitten by grief, they no longer knew what was to be done.

sanskrit: vrīḍāṃ jagmuḥ purā yāḥ sma sakhīnām api yoṣitaḥ tā ekavastrā nirlajjāḥ śvaśrūṇāṃ purato 'bhavan
english: Women who once had felt shame even before their own companions now stood, clad in a single garment and stripped of all modesty, in the presence of their mothers-in-law.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ susūkṣmeṣu śokeṣv āśvāsayan sma yāḥ tāḥ śokavihvalā rājann upaikṣanta parasparam
english: Those who once consoled one another in the slightest sorrows now, overcome with grief, O king, paid no heed to one another at all.

sanskrit: tābhiḥ parivṛto rājā rudatībhiḥ sahasraśaḥ niryayau nagarād dīnas tūrṇam āyodhanaṃ prati
english: Encircled by those women weeping in their thousands, the wretched king set forth in haste from the city toward the field of battle.

sanskrit: śilpino vaṇijo vaiśyāḥ sarvakarmopajīvinaḥ te pārthivaṃ puraskṛtya niryayur nagarād bahiḥ
english: Artisans, merchants, and traders, and all who lived by every kind of craft, placing the king at their head, went forth out of the city.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ vikrośamānānām ārtānāṃ kurusaṃkṣaye prādurāsīn mahāñ śabdo vyathayan bhuvanāny uta
english: From those women crying out in their anguish at the ruin of the Kurus there arose a mighty clamor that shook the very worlds.

sanskrit: yugāntakāle saṃprāpte bhūtānāṃ dahyatām iva abhāvaḥ syād ayaṃ prāpta iti bhūtāni menire
english: As though the time of the world's ending had come and all creatures were being consumed, living beings thought that the hour of universal dissolution was upon them.

sanskrit: bhṛśam udvignamanasas te paurāḥ kurusaṃkṣaye prākrośanta mahārāja svanuraktās tadā bhṛśam
english: Their hearts deeply troubled at the ruin of the Kurus, the townsfolk, devoted as they were, cried out then most bitterly, O great king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca krośamātraṃ tato gatvā dadṛśus tān mahārathān śāradvataṃ kṛpaṃ drauṇiṃ kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having gone but a krośa's distance, they beheld those great chariot-warriors: Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat, the son of Droṇa, and Kṛtavarman as well.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvaiva rājānaṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram aśrukaṇṭhā viniḥśvasya rudantam idam abruvan
english: And they, on seeing the king, that lord whose only sight was wisdom, sighing with throats choked by tears, spoke thus to him as he wept.

sanskrit: putras tava mahārāja kṛtvā karma suduṣkaram gataḥ sānucaro rājañ śakralokaṃ mahīpatiḥ
english: "Your son, O great king, having wrought a most arduous deed, has gone, O king, together with his followers, to the world of Indra, that guardian of the earth."

sanskrit: duryodhanabalān muktā vayam eva trayo rathāḥ sarvam anyat parikṣīṇaṃ sainyaṃ te bharatarṣabha
english: "Of Duryodhana's host we three chariot-warriors alone are left; all the rest of your army has perished utterly, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā rājānaṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tadā gāndhārīṃ putraśokārtām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having thus spoken to the king, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat then addressed these words to Gāndhārī, stricken with grief for her sons.

sanskrit: abhītā yudhyamānās te ghnantaḥ śatrugaṇān bahūn vīrakarmāṇi kurvāṇāḥ putrās te nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Fighting without fear, slaying many hosts of foes and performing the deeds of heroes, your sons have met their death."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ saṃprāpya lokāṃs te nirmalāñ śastranirjitān bhāsvaraṃ deham āsthāya viharanty amarā iva
english: "Surely, having attained the stainless worlds won by their weapons, and taking on radiant bodies, they now disport themselves like the immortals."

sanskrit: na hi kaś cid dhi śūrāṇāṃ yudhyamānaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ śastreṇa nidhanaṃ prāpto na ca kaś cit kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: "For not one of those heroes met death by the sword while fighting with his back turned, nor while standing with palms joined in surrender."

sanskrit: etāṃ tāṃ kṣatriyasyāhuḥ purāṇāṃ paramāṃ gatim śastreṇa nidhanaṃ saṃkhye tān na śocitum arhasi
english: "This they call the ancient and supreme goal of the warrior: death by the sword in battle. You ought not to grieve for them."

sanskrit: na cāpi śatravas teṣām ṛdhyante rājñi pāṇḍavāḥ śṛṇu yat kṛtam asmābhir aśvatthāmapurogamaiḥ
english: "Nor do their foes, the Pāṇḍavas, O queen, prosper either. Hear what we have done, with Aśvatthāman at our head."

sanskrit: adharmeṇa hataṃ śrutvā bhīmasenena te sutam suptaṃ śibiram āviśya pāṇḍūnāṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam
english: "On hearing that your son had been slain unjustly by Bhīmasena, we entered the sleeping camp of the Pāṇḍavas and wrought havoc there."

sanskrit: pāñcālā nihatāḥ sarve dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ drupadasyātmajāś caiva draupadeyāś ca pātitāḥ
english: "All the Pāñcālas were slain, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head; the sons of Drupada and the sons of Draupadī too were struck down."

sanskrit: tathā viśasanaṃ kṛtvā putraśatrugaṇasya te prādravāma raṇe sthātuṃ na hi śakyāmahe trayaḥ
english: "Having thus made slaughter of the host of your sons' foes, we fled; for we three could not stand in the field."

sanskrit: te hi śūrā maheṣvāsāḥ kṣipram eṣyanti pāṇḍavāḥ amarṣavaśam āpannā vairaṃ pratijihīrṣavaḥ
english: "For those heroic Pāṇḍavas, mighty archers, will come swiftly, fallen under the sway of wrath and eager to requite the feud."

sanskrit: nihatān ātmajāñ śrutvā pramattān puruṣarṣabhāḥ ninīṣantaḥ padaṃ śūrāḥ kṣipram eva yaśasvini
english: "Hearing that their sons were slain while off their guard, those bulls among men, those heroes, eager to track us down, will come at once, O illustrious lady."

sanskrit: pāṇḍūnāṃ kilbiṣaṃ kṛtvā saṃsthātuṃ notsahāmahe anujānīhi no rājñi mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Having done this wrong to the Pāṇḍavas, we dare not remain. Grant us leave, O queen, and set not your heart upon grief."

sanskrit: rājaṃs tvam anujānīhi dhairyam ātiṣṭha cottamam niṣṭhāntaṃ paśya cāpi tvaṃ kṣatradharmaṃ ca kevalam
english: "Grant us leave, O king, and take your stand upon the highest fortitude; behold too the warrior's duty, fulfilled to its very end."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā rājānaṃ kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam kṛpaś ca kṛtavarmā ca droṇaputraś ca bhārata
english: Having thus spoken to the king and made the reverent circuit about him, Kṛpa, Kṛtavarman, and the son of Droṇa, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇā rājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam gaṅgām anu mahātmānas tūrṇam aśvān acodayan
english: gazing back upon the wise king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, those great-souled men urged their horses swiftly along the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: apakramya tu te rājan sarva eva mahārathāḥ āmantryānyonyam udvignās tridhā te prayayus tataḥ
english: And having withdrawn, O king, all those great chariot-warriors, troubled at heart, took leave of one another and then departed by three separate ways.

sanskrit: jagāma hāstinapuraṃ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tadā svam eva rāṣṭraṃ hārdikyo drauṇir vyāsāśramaṃ yayau
english: Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat went then to Hāstinapura, Hārdikya to his own kingdom, and the son of Droṇa journeyed to the hermitage of Vyāsa.

sanskrit: evaṃ te prayayur vīrā vīkṣamāṇāḥ parasparam bhayārtāḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇām āgaskṛtvā mahātmanām
english: Thus those heroes departed, glancing at one another, stricken with fear, for they had done a wrong against the great-souled sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: sametya vīrā rājānaṃ tadā tv anudite ravau viprajagmur mahārāja yathecchakam ariṃdamāḥ
english: Having met with the king while the sun had not yet risen, those heroes, those tamers of foes, then parted, each going his own way as he wished, O great king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hateṣu sarvasainyeṣu dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śuśruve pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ niryātaṃ gajasāhvayāt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When all the armies had been slain, the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira heard that his aged father had set forth from the City of the Elephant.

sanskrit: so 'bhyayāt putraśokārtaḥ putraśokapariplutam śocamāno mahārāja bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitas tadā
english: He went forth to meet him, himself stricken with grief for his sons, to that king likewise overwhelmed with grief for his sons; mourning, O great king, he went then together with his brothers.
